name: Systematic Index Volatility Premium Capture Program (VPD/VPN-style)
summary: A rules-based, calendar-driven program that sells index volatility on a fixed schedule in fixed size - the retail, defined-risk analogue of the CBOE VPD and VPN benchmark indices - rather than a single discretionary trade.

legs.strike_rule: monthly cycle: short SPY put at |delta| 0.15-0.20, opened on a fixed calendar day
long SPY put at short strike - W (W = $5 on SPY), making every cycle defined-risk
optional second side for the strangle version: short SPY call at delta 0.15-0.20
long SPY call at short call strike + W

max_profit: Total credit per cycle; the program's return is the compounded sum of cycles, not any single trade
max_loss: Per cycle: (W x 100) - credit per side. Program-level: the cumulative drawdown from consecutive losing cycles, which is the number that actually matters and must be simulated before launch.
breakevens: Per cycle, short strike -/+ credit per share; program-level breakeven is a hit rate, not a price

greeks.delta: small and mean-reverting around zero across cycles
greeks.gamma: negative, concentrated in the final week of each cycle
greeks.theta: positive and steady - the program's entire return source
greeks.vega: negative; the program is implicitly short the variance risk premium

typical_dte: 30-45 DTE per cycle, 12 cycles per year
when_to_use: When the objective is a benchmark-like exposure to the equity variance risk premium rather than trade selection - the systematic complement to the bank's discretionary short-premium entries. The named CBOE benchmarks (VPD, VPN) trade VIX futures options, which are not available on Alpaca, so this is a documented equivalent on SPY, not a replication.
entry_rules: Fixed schedule: open one cycle on the first trading day after monthly opex, every month, without a market-view gate. The absence of discretion is the strategy.
Defined risk always: every short leg must carry a long wing. The naked benchmark versions are level 4 and are not permitted here.
Size per cycle: total defined risk <= 2% of equity. Twelve cycles a year at 2% is the program's risk budget; it must not be scaled up after winning months.
Skip rule (the only discretion allowed): skip the cycle entirely if VIX spot > 35 at the scheduled open, and resume the next month. Log every skip.
Strangle version only when IV rank >= 30; otherwise run the put side alone.
SPY only. OI >= 1000 per leg. One MLeg order per side.
Program-level circuit breaker: if trailing 6-cycle cumulative P/L is worse than -6% of equity, halt the program and require a review before restarting.
management_rules: Per cycle: take profit at 50% of credit, time stop at 21 DTE, loss stop at 2x credit.
Never roll a losing cycle into the next one - each cycle is independent by design, and rolling destroys the benchmark property.
Never add a second cycle in the same month to make back a loss.
Record per-cycle credit, realized P/L, and the SPY move, so the program's realized premium capture can be compared to the variance risk premium it is supposed to harvest.
exit_rules: Force-close every cycle by 15:45 ET on its expiration day.
Close any short leg at extrinsic < $0.10, |delta| >= 0.85, or when ITM by more than 0.25 x its wing width.
Ex-dividend guard on any short call side before every SPY ex-dividend date while ITM.
A cycle that hits the loss stop is closed in full, both sides, not just the tested side.
assignment_risk: One or two short legs per cycle, each covered by a wing of the same right and expiry, so every assignment is defined - but SPY is share-settled and a 100-share assignment is about $60k against a $50k account. The expiration-day flatten is what makes the program safe to run unattended.
buying_power: (W x 100) - credit per side, per cycle; at 2% of equity per cycle that is $1,000 held on $50k.
liquidity_needs: SPY monthlies - the deepest options market available.
common_mistakes: Adding discretion once losses appear, which turns a benchmark program into a discretionary book with worse selection; scaling up after good months; skipping the program-level circuit breaker; claiming it replicates VPD/VPN when the underlying exposure (SPY vs VIX futures) is fundamentally different.
zero_dte_notes: Not applicable - the program is defined by its monthly cadence. A daily 0DTE version is a completely different risk object with far worse tails.
family: Completeness gap-fill (cross-family): ratio/naked-financed put and call structures, quantity-unbalanced condors and strangles, stock+option overlays and monetizations, capital-protection and hybrid builds, 0DTE four-leg income, volatility-surface and relative-value trades, event-driven overlays, and roll/adjustment structures
